steps.observation: You have 30 seconds. Explain the difference between RNA and DNA.

steps.action:
DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid)
• Sugar: Deoxyribose (lacks one O on the 2′ carbon).  
• Bases: A, G, C, T (thymine).  
• Structure: Usually double-stranded helix; long, stable.  
• Location/function: Stores genetic blueprint; mostly in nucleus (and mitochondria).

RNA (ribonucleic acid)
• Sugar: Ribose (has 2′-OH group).  
• Bases: A, G, C, U (uracil replaces T).  
• Structure: Usually single-stranded; shorter, folds into varied shapes; less stable.  
• Location/function: Acts as working copies and tools—mRNA (messenger), rRNA (ribosomal), tRNA (transfer), and many regulatory types—mainly in nucleus & cytoplasm.

Key points: DNA = long-term, double-helix, thymine, deoxyribose. RNA = short-term, single-strand, uracil, ribose, versatile roles.
